title: Availability Zones, Availability Sets and Scale Sets

header.html: Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20-25%)
Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets; deploy and configure Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
the official Microsoft Learn AZ-104 study guide, skills measured as of October 26, 2023

html:
1Why availability options

A single VM can fail from hardware faults or planned maintenance. Azure offers placement options so some instances stay up.

Option Protects against VM SLA (typical)
Single VM with Premium SSD disks Little 99.9%
Availability set Rack and maintenance failures inside one datacenter 99.95%
Availability zones A whole datacenter (zone) failure 99.99%

[Verify live] SLA percentages.

2Availability zones

An availability zone is a physically separate location (own power, cooling, network) within a region. Regions that support zones have at least three.

Fact Detail
Zonal service You pick the zone for a VM, disk or IP (for example zone 1)
Zone-redundant service Azure spreads automatically across zones (for example zone-redundant storage, Standard load balancer)
Set at creation A VM's zone is chosen when you create it; to change it you recreate it

3Availability sets

An availability set places VMs across fault domains and update domains in one datacenter.

Concept Meaning
Fault domain A group sharing power and network (a rack); VMs spread across up to 3
Update domain A group rebooted together during planned maintenance; up to 20

You choose the set when creating the VM; you cannot add an existing VM to a set (recreate it). Put each tier (web, app) in its own set behind a load balancer.

Exam tip

. Zones protect against datacenter failure; availability sets protect against rack and maintenance events inside a datacenter. A VM cannot be in both a zone and an availability set.

4Virtual Machine Scale Sets

A Virtual Machine Scale Set (VMSS) deploys and manages a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that can scale out and in automatically.

Feature Fact
Autoscale Rules on metrics (for example CPU above 70% for 10 minutes: add 2 instances) or schedules
Limits Set minimum, maximum and default instance counts
Scale out / in Add / remove instances (horizontal)
Orchestration modes Flexible (recommended, mixes VM types, spread across zones) and Uniform (identical instances)
Load balancing Use an Azure Load Balancer or Application Gateway in front
Health and repair Health probes and automatic instance repairs
Updates Upgrade policy (automatic, rolling, manual) updates the model and the instances

Exam tip

. "Add VMs automatically when CPU is high and remove them when load drops" = Virtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale rules.

Exam tip

. Pick zones for datacenter failure, availability sets for rack and maintenance, scale sets for automatic capacity; do not combine a zone with an availability set.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A workload must survive the failure of an entire datacenter in the region. What should be used?

  • AAvailability zones
  • BA single VM
  • CAn availability set
  • DA larger VM size
Show the answer

Answer: A. Zones are separate datacenters in the region.

S2VMs must be protected from rack failures and planned maintenance in one datacenter. What should be used?

  • AA resource lock
  • BAn availability set
  • CA budget
  • DA tag
Show the answer

Answer: B. Fault and update domains protect against those events.

S3An existing VM must be added to an availability set. What is the correct action?

  • ARecreate the VM in the availability set
  • BAdd it from the portal by editing the availability set
  • CResize it to a size that supports availability sets
  • DRename it so that it matches the availability set
Show the answer

Answer: A. A VM can only be placed in a set when it is created.

S4A web tier should add instances automatically when CPU exceeds 70 percent. Which service fits?

  • AAn availability set with fault domains and update domains
  • BA single VM with Premium SSD disks and a large size
  • CAzure Backup of each VM to a Recovery Services vault
  • DVirtual Machine Scale Set with autoscale
Show the answer

Answer: D. Scale sets support metric-based autoscale.

S5What is a fault domain?

  • AA group of VMs rebooted together during planned maintenance events
  • BA region that contains at least three physically separate datacenters
  • CA group of VMs sharing power and network, such as a rack
  • DA subscription that holds the VMs of one application tier
Show the answer

Answer: C. Fault domains share hardware infrastructure.

S6Which option gives the highest typical VM availability SLA?

  • AAvailability zones
  • BAvailability sets
  • CA single VM
  • DA stopped VM
Show the answer

Answer: A. Zones provide 99.99 percent.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What does an availability zone protect against?

Show the answer

The failure of a whole datacenter.

R2What is an update domain?

Show the answer

A group of VMs rebooted together during planned maintenance.

R3How many fault domains can an availability set use?

Show the answer

Up to three.

R4What triggers autoscale in a scale set?

Show the answer

Metric rules or schedules.

R5Which orchestration mode is recommended?

Show the answer

Flexible.

R6Can a VM be in an availability set and a zone?

Show the answer

No.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Zones separate datacenters, 99.99%, chosen at creation
Availability sets fault + update domains, 99.95%, chosen at creation
Scale sets identical VMs, autoscale by metric or schedule, flexible mode, health repair
